correctness.rationale: Finite equivalence classes are characterized by the cardinalities of their selected intersections, and global extension is equivalent to matching complete original class capacities. This gives exact full and extendible rank-polynomial coefficients. Any capacity-crossing pair forces at least the smallest positive original size gap omissions; at equality, one truncated larger class is forced on each side, and selected-profile balance forces a common nearest-size pair. Counting the wrong pairings gives the displayed integer first-defect coefficient. A separate executable verifies all formulas for every partition through six vertices, using restrictions of explicitly enumerated full automorphisms, and first-defect counts for every nonuniform partition of seven vertices.

value.rationale: The first failure of same-host homogeneity is an intrinsic structure-size threshold. It is exactly the smallest difference between occurring equivalence-class sizes; the formula counts every obstruction at that precise boundary, and coupled rank profiles distinguish local partial symmetries from globally realizable ones for any nonuniform finite partition. This complete natural structural invariant is not an arbitrary finite slice or rebranding of the all-equal case.
